doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: The singing girl on the CD cover; 51 years in education
summary: Jordan taught a bashful girl 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' on the day of the session; Rowe congratulates him on 51 years in education.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah. You know there’s a little quote here on this CD, and I’m not sure you said this but you can tell me.
I might have forgot what I said.
It says, “very special thanks to all who make this time a joy to be living in.” Do you remember saying that?
Okay. I didn’t know if you said that or not.
But now there’s another thing that I’m really proud of. See that little girl on the cover of that?

I was walking and she said, “Mister, you play music?” I say, “yeah.” She said, “I would like to know how to sing.” So I taught her “Mary Had a Little Lamb” out there and they had a little group of children out there. And that really touched my heart. I stopped and said, “all right listen you want to sing?” She wanted to learn how to sing. And she was so bashful and she was just so withdrawn and when I left I was there about ten or fifteen minutes and she was singing and a whole little group of them were singing, and it felt so good. I said now that really made my day because I was feeling bad about the session. But that made my day. I said now at least, maybe this is what I was supposed to do today. And it felt good and me dealing with kids I mean that’s a natural thing. When the little girl said she would want to learn how to sing, and me I would stop and say all right, we’re going to sing a song. You want to learn how to sing? I’m going to teach you how to sing. So I started “Mary Had a Little Lamb” and maybe went into some other little nursery rhyme. And she got it down. I said now this is it, this made my day. So I guess that’s the teacher’s part in me.
I guess so. It’s natural for you. Well I want to congratulate you on your 51 years in education.
Right. 71 years old. © Fillius Jazz Archive -27-
Going half strong, I’m not strong as I used to be but I’m half strong.
Well in listening to this recording and seeing what you do with the kids, you’ve still got a lot of energy.
Well, trying to keep it going.
